**What I did and why**

I read Microsoft's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and checked the live quote, then bought MSFT within your mandate. Microsoft's results support a purchase: **total revenue for fiscal 2024 was $245,122 million (≈$245.1 billion), up 16% from $211,915 million**, driven by growth in every segment — Intelligent Cloud revenue up 20% to $105.4 billion (Azure and other cloud services +30%) and Microsoft Cloud revenue up 23% to $137.4 billion. Profitability and cash generation were equally strong: operating income $109,433 million (+24%), net income $88,136 million (+22%), diluted EPS $11.80 (+22%), and operating cash flow $118,548 million (up $31.0 billion), a very low-risk balance sheet with $75.5 billion in cash and short-term investments. The main blemishes were modest ones — a $28.9 billion IRS transfer-pricing proposed adjustment that Microsoft is contesting, heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5 billion), and continued tight margins in the Activision-inclusive gaming business (a ~$1.4 billion operating loss contribution since acquisition) — but none of these overturn the growth and cash-flow picture. With the stock quoting $420.18 last ($420.16 bid / $420.20 ask) at 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06, I placed a single limit buy of **23 shares at $420.20, which filled** — a total of about $9,665, inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and well under the account's $50,000 cash, with no funds moved out of the account.
